title: Danish residence and work permit under the Pay Limit Scheme: a job offer with annual pay of at least DKK 552,000 (2026)

sources.title: Aliens Act (consolidated Act No. 953 of 2026), § 9 a(2)(3) and (29): a job offer with annual pay of at least DKK 400,000, adjusted each year in line with wage growth and rounded to DKK 1,000
SIRI, the Pay Limit Scheme: the pay limit is DKK 552,000 a year for 2026, set each 1 January; only cash pay, pension and paid holiday allowance count; pay and terms usual in Denmark
Aliens Act, § 9 a(9), (10), (25) and (26): at least 30 hours a week; pay into a Danish bank account; no permit for a job in a lawful labour dispute or for an offer that is not genuine
Aliens Act, § 9 a(4): the permit requires that the principal and the family members who get permits through them receive no assistance under the Active Social Policy Act
Aliens Act, § 9 m(1): where essential business or employment interests favour it, a family member of a foreigner with a § 9 a(2) permit may get one, if they share a home
SIRI, accompanying family of employees: a spouse or registered partner, a cohabiting partner over 18 after at least 1.5 to 2 years living together, and a child under 18
Aliens Act, §§ 1 and 2: citizens of Finland, Iceland, Norway and Sweden live in Denmark without a permit; EU and EEA citizens fall under the EU rules on free movement
EU Residence Order (Order No. 1457 of 2020), §§ 1(2) and 2(2): Swiss citizens are treated like EU citizens under the EU rules on free movement
Guardianship Act (consolidated Act No. 1122 of 2021), § 1(1): children and young people under 18 who have not married are minors
Order No. 1612 of 2025 on fees, § 5(2)(1): for 1 January to 31 December 2026 the fee for a permit application under Aliens Act § 9 a(2)(1) to (9) and (11) to (14) is DKK 6,810
Order No. 1612 of 2025 on fees, § 5(5)(1): for 1 January to 31 December 2026 the fee for a permit application under Aliens Act § 9 m(1) and (2), for family members, is DKK 3,080
Aliens Act, § 9 h(1)(4) and (9) and (2): a fee is paid no later than with an application under § 9 a(2)(1) to (14) or § 9 m(1); the minister sets the fees
SIRI, the Pay Limit Scheme: normal processing time 1 month, up to 3 months if more information is needed; a permit for the employment period, normally 4 years at most

requirements.title: Not a citizen of Denmark, another Nordic country, an EU or EEA state or Switzerland: they live and work in Denmark without this permit

assessments.title: A job offer in Denmark with annual pay of at least the pay limit: DKK 400,000 in the act, adjusted each year for wage growth; DKK 552,000 for 2026 as SIRI publishes it
Employment of at least 30 hours a week
Pay goes into a Danish bank account, opened within 180 days of entry or of the permit by someone who does not yet hold a permit of at least 180 days
Pay and employment terms not inferior to the Danish standards of the professional field
No permit for a job covered by a lawful labour dispute, nor where the actual employment is presumed not to match the application or the offer mainly serves to obtain residence
Neither the principal nor the family members with permits through them receive assistance under the Active Social Policy Act
Family members live at the same address as the principal and receive no assistance under the Active Social Policy Act

dependents.title: Spouse who was 18 or more at the wedding; married younger, both now 18 or more: possible, as a cohabiting partner after at least 1.5 to 2 years living together
Cohabiting partner over 18: SIRI asks, as a rule, for at least 1.5 to 2 years living together, so 2 years or more counts, and 1.5 to 2 years, or a registered partnership, is possible

costs.title: Fee for the Pay Limit Scheme permit application: DKK 6,810, the amount set for 1 January to 31 December 2026
Fee for each accompanying family member's permit application: DKK 3,080, the amount set for 1 January to 31 December 2026

durations.title: SIRI's processing of the application: normally 1 month, up to 3 months if further information is needed
Permit valid for the period of the employment; for an employment of 4 years or more, normally 4 years, then extended
